stories.headline: Revisiting 2026 preseason bold predictions for 32 NFL teams: Which are on track?
stories.summary: In the preseason, we made bold predictions for every NFL team, from Jordan Love's MVP case to Isaiah Likely's catch total. Which ones are on track? Which seem unlikely?
stories.body:
Part of making preseason predictions is seeing how those forecasts actually fare. It's easy to predict something, but we also need to check on our predictions and hold ourselves accountable.

Before Week 1, I made one bold prediction for every NFL team as part of our lookahead to the 2026 season. These were big swings -- things I thought could happen but would be upsets if they did. And five weeks into the season, we've learned a lot.

That makes this a great time to dive back into those preview predictions and find out how things are going. Which ones are on track? Which might still happen? And which were so far off that we might as well scrap them for a completely new one? In some cases, five weeks means everything has changed. In others, not so much.

Let's take a look and see where we stand for all 32 teams.

Jump to a team:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

On target

Buffalo Bills
Original prediction: Wide receiver Keon Coleman will record 750 or more receiving yards and at least five touchdowns -- both career highs.

Why it's on target: Coleman had been on a bit of a production tear on plays when DJ Moore was off the field until Monday night, when he managed only 7 receiving yards in a game that Moore missed. Still, Coleman's 224 receiving yards so far put him on pace for 761 yards over a full season. If Moore -- who did not play Monday due to a shoulder injury -- misses more time, that will help Coleman's cause. Not playing the Rams every week should, too.

Jacksonville Jaguars
Original prediction: Cornerback Montaric Brown will record a worse-than-average yards allowed per coverage snap (1.1 per NFL Next Gen Stats).

Why it's on target: Considering Brown is at 3.8 yards allowed per coverage snap, we're well on our way. The idea for this prediction was that Brown's strong 2025 campaign was fueled by on-ball results that tend not to be stable from year to year and that he would regress in 2026. So far, that looks right. Brown has missed all but six snaps in the past two games due to a hamstring injury.

New York Giants
Original prediction: Tight end Isaiah Likely will lead the team in receptions.

Why it's on target: Likely currently leads the Giants in receptions, with 33 catches to Malik Nabers' 29. As Nabers continues to recover from the ACL injury he suffered last season, he might accrue more volume. But Likely is ahead right now and has proved to be a key part of this new Giants offense.

Tennessee Titans
Original prediction: Cornerback Alontae Taylor will allow 1.4 yards per coverage snap or worse, per NFL Next Gen Stats.

Why it's on target: Taylor is right on target at 1.4. Should that continue, this would be disappointing for the Titans after they signed Taylor in free agency following a 1.0 yards-per-coverage-snap season in 2025. But Taylor was at 1.6 in 2023 and 2024, which is a big reason I made this prediction. For context, the average for an outside cornerback is 1.1.

Still a chance ...

Arizona Cardinals
Original prediction: The Cardinals will go 1-16.

Why there's still a chance: I don't think this will hit anymore, especially since the Cardinals won their opener. But I won't quite throw this out yet because Arizona's remaining schedule is an absolute gauntlet. There could be winnable games against the Commanders, Jets and Saints down the road, but if the Cardinals can't win any of those, I could get the backdoor cover.

Atlanta Falcons
Original prediction: Safety Xavier Watts will be a first- or second-team All-Pro.

Why there's still a chance: Watts has one interception, one forced fumble and a half-sack as part of a Falcons defense that has been better than expected. He has allowed 0.8 yards per coverage snap -- higher than average for a safety, though I don't put a lot of stock in that number for safeties considering the variety and complexity of assignments at that position. This is a long shot, but you never know -- if Watts goes on an interception run, anything could happen.

Baltimore Ravens
Original prediction: The Ravens' defense will rank in the top four in EPA per play.

Why there's still a chance: Baltimore ranks 17th through five games. That's not ideal for making the top four, but it doesn't put the Ravens out of the running just yet, as we've seen their defenses turn it around in the second half of the season in recent years. Considering the talent the Ravens have and that they are playing under a new coach with a defensive background in Jesse Minter, I think it's at least feasible. Trey Hendrickson, who ranks sixth in pass rush win rate at edge, has missed the past two games due to a broken finger that required surgery. If Baltimore can get him back, that should help.

Carolina Panthers
Original prediction: The Panthers will finish last in the NFC South.
Why there's still a chance: Considering how well Carolina's offense has played, I sincerely doubt that I will be correct on this. But this is the NFC South, and you just never know. The Panthers are only 1.5 games out of last place, and I have a strong opinion of cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, so their absences could really sting.

Cincinnati Bengals
Original prediction: Running back Chase Brown will record at least 15 total touchdowns.

Why there's still a chance: With only one score thus far, this prediction is off to a pretty rough start. But a big part of why I backed Brown was the Bengals having the easiest schedule in the NFL. The beginning of that schedule wasn't easy, and it gets lighter from here, so there should be plenty more touchdowns to come.

Cleveland Browns
Original prediction: Quarterback Taylen Green will start at least four games.

Why there's still a chance: The odds have dropped. I had figured the Browns would already be on to Shedeur Sanders by this point. Even though Deshaun Watson hasn't been quite as bad as expected, I still think that the Browns will make the move to Sanders relatively soon and that an end-of-year stint for Green remains in play.

Dallas Cowboys
Original prediction: Kicker Brandon Aubrey will record the most field goals over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats.

Why there's still a chance: Aubrey is off to a slower start than I would have guessed, with 1.3 field goals made over expectation. That ranks 13th, and he has missed a PAT, too. But there's still plenty of time for him to move to the top.

Denver Broncos
Original prediction: Cornerback Riley Moss will command a $17 million-per-year contract after this season, either with the Broncos or someone else.

Why there's still a chance: Moss missed Week 5 with a rib injury, but he has allowed 1.1 yards per coverage snap (average) this season, per NFL Next Gen Stats. He picked off Trevor Lawrence in Denver's Week 2 win over the Jaguars but was also burned badly by Konata Mumpfield on a double move for a 48-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter against the Rams in Week 3. I still feel good about this one, though.

Detroit Lions
Original prediction: Edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson will win Defensive Player of the Year.

Why there's still a chance: Four sacks and a 66th percentile pass rush win rate at edge isn't a bad start, but he's going to have to pick it up to fulfill this prediction. He has the talent level to do it, but the fact that the rest of the Lions' defense is looking so weak is going to hurt Hutchinson's sack total, which in turn will hurt his DPOY chances.

Green Bay Packers
Original prediction: Quarterback Jordan Love will finish in the top three in MVP voting.

Why there's still a chance: I was prepared to throw this one out ... until Week 5, when Love posted a 94 QBR in the Packers' 31-7 dismantling of the Bears. It's still a long shot given his slow start, but Love has battled through Green Bay's disastrous pass protection. And those first four weeks could have gone a lot worse considering the lack of a running game and how much duress Love was under. The Packers are more pass-heavy this season, too, so I'll hold out hope.

Houston Texans
Original prediction: Wide receiver Nico Collins will record at least 1,500 receiving yards.

Why there's still a chance: Even though he missed two games, Collins is not far off the pace. He has 249 receiving yards over three games, which puts him on pace for 1,245 receiving yards over 15 games, which is how many he'd play if he doesn't miss any more time. There's an outside shot. But Sunday's acquisition of Marvin Harrison Jr. probably doesn't help the odds.

Indianapolis Colts
Original prediction: Either Sauce Gardner or Charvarius Ward will be a first-team All-Pro cornerback.

Why there's still a chance: Ward has put up solid numbers to start the season, allowing 0.8 yards per coverage snap (better than the 1.1 average for an outside corner) and minus-4.7 EPA when targeted, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Gardner hasn't fared nearly as well, but it's too early to count this one out.

Las Vegas Raiders
Original prediction: Tight end Brock Bowers will win Offensive Player of the Year.

Why there's still a chance: Missing the first two games of the season will hurt Bowers' case, but he has been pretty amazing since hitting the field: 24 receptions for 312 receiving yards and three touchdowns. That pace will put him right in the mix for the award.

Los Angeles Rams
Original prediction: Tight end Terrance Ferguson will catch eight touchdown passes.

Why there's still a chance: On one hand, this seems like a long shot since Ferguson is on IR with an ankle injury. But the Ferguson bull case thesis essentially hit when he was on the field. With Puka Nacua out in Week 2, Ferguson got nine targets and caught six passes, including one for a touchdown. The preseason question was whether Ferguson could become the Rams' third receiving option -- and the No. 2 guy if either Nacua or Davante Adams was out. If Ferguson is healthy, it seems like the answer is yes. That keeps this prediction alive.

New England Patriots
Original prediction: The Patriots will trade for an edge rusher before the trade deadline.

Why there's still a chance: Even though Harold Landry III hasn't played yet this season, the Patriots are in better shape at edge rusher than I thought before the season thanks to the emergence of Elijah Ponder, who has 4.5 sacks and is in the 49th percentile in pass rush win rate at edge. Still, New England could absolutely want to upgrade at the deadline.

New Orleans Saints
Original prediction: Jordyn Tyson will be a top-15 wide receiver in terms of fantasy points per game.

Why there's still a chance: Tyson has yet to play due to the hamstring injury we knew would sideline him for the first part of the season when I made this prediction. So ... we still have a chance since this is about rate, not totals.

New York Jets
Original prediction: The Jets will sign defensive tackle Jowon Briggs to an extension before the end of the season.

Why there's still a chance: Briggs is part of a Jets defensive tackle rotation that includes Harrison Phillips, T'Vondre Sweat and Darrell Jackson Jr. Briggs has two sacks this season and an average pass rush win rate for a starting interior lineman, but his run stop win rate has taken a big step back, dropping from 85th percentile in 2025 to 12th percentile this season. It's that figure which could give New York pause.

Philadelphia Eagles
Original prediction: Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard will record at least 0.8 sacks per game.

Why there's still a chance: We're just getting started. Greenard began his season in Week 3, played two games, then was inactive with an ankle injury in Week 5. He has yet to record a sack, but the Eagles have been easing him into the lineup. Assuming Greenard gets healthy and the Eagles ramp him up to a full workload, he'll have a shot -- albeit a smaller one than before the season began.

Pittsburgh Steelers

Original prediction: Tight end Darnell Washington will score five or more touchdowns.

Why there's still a chance: Washington has one touchdown thus far, but we have a real shot here considering how enticing he can be in the red zone as a 6-foot-7, 264-pound target. His route rate has ticked up a little compared to last season, too.

San Francisco 49ers
Original prediction: Rookie running back Kaelon Black will record at least 650 rushing yards as the 49ers -- for real this time -- take it easy on Christian McCaffrey's workload.

Why there's still a chance: The 49ers really are backing off McCaffrey's carry share. Last season, he rushed the ball on 71% of San Francisco's designed rush attempts. That number is down to 52% this season. And Black is the clear No. 2, with 136 rushing yards thus far. If McCaffrey misses any time, Black should be a lock to hit this prediction. And there's a chance it happens even if McCaffrey stays healthy.

Throw it out, start over

Chicago Bears
Original prediction: The Bears will lead the league in team open score. It's a metric the team was middle-of-the-road in a year ago.

Why we're throwing it out: Entering Week 5, the Bears ranked 19th in team open score.

New bold prediction: Offensive tackle Darnell Wright will finish in the top five in Protector of the Year voting. Wright currently has pass block and run block win rates in the 79th and 52nd percentiles at tackle, respectively, so he has work to do. But getting himself onto Protector of the Year ballots is possible, especially if the Bears' offense takes off again once Caleb Williams gets back on the field.

Kansas City Chiefs
Original prediction: Wide receiver Rashee Rice will stay healthy and collect 1,300 receiving yards.

Why we're throwing it out: A hamstring injury forced Rice out of the Chiefs' Week 4 win over the Raiders before he had a catch. It's possible he won't miss any more time since the Chiefs' bye was in Week 5, but with only 190 receiving yards so far, Rice is well behind the necessary pace to get to 1,300 yards.

New bold prediction: Rice will reach 1,100 receiving yards. Same bet, just a lower bar that would still be a career high by a decent margin. Rice recorded more than 80 receiving yards in two of the three games he played before the hamstring injury, and Kansas City ranks fourth in pass rate over expectation despite having a very strong run game. The Chiefs will still be a pass-heavy offense, which should provide Rice plenty of opportunity to hit this number.

Los Angeles Chargers
Original prediction: Offensive tackle Joe Alt will win Protector of the Year.

Why we're throwing it out: He hasn't been nearly good enough. Alt has recorded pass block and run block win rates in the 67th and 38th percentiles at tackle, respectively. But more important, he leads the league in penalties with six. He missed the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos with a neck injury, too.

New bold prediction: Cornerback Tarheeb Still will deserve to make the Pro Bowl but won't make the original team. Instead, he'll earn a spot on ESPN's snubs list. Still is off to a nice start to the season, allowing 0.8 yards per coverage snap and a minus-8% completion percentage over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. He won't get the recognition because he's not a huge name and plays for the disappointing Chargers, but I think his strong season will continue.

Miami Dolphins
Original prediction: Quarterback Malik Willis will finish in the top 12 in QBR.

Why we're throwing it out: Willis currently ranks 24th. He has had his moments, and I'm not giving up on him having long-term success with the Dolphins. But I don't think top 12 is realistic for this season.

New bold prediction: Wide receiver Chris Bell will record at least 700 receiving yards. It's remarkable that he's already playing considering he tore an ACL in November. He has only 92 receiving yards thus far but has 234 incomplete air yards, per NFL Next Gen Stats, 14th most in the NFL. I expect he'll convert some of those air yards into actual yards at a higher rate going forward.

Minnesota Vikings
Original prediction: Quarterback Kyler Murray will finish in the top 12 in QBR.
Why we're throwing it out: Entering Week 5, Murray was last in QBR. After the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints, he has moved all the way up to ... 27th. Even though I'm hopeful Murray will improve as the season goes on, I don't think he'll be able to get to the top 12.

New bold prediction: Linebacker Blake Cashman will record at least nine sacks. This would be a heck of a number for an off-ball linebacker, but Cashman rushes the passer a ton in Brian Flores' scheme (32% of dropbacks) and already has 2.5 sacks.

Seattle Seahawks
Original prediction: Jadarian Price will finish the season as a top-eight running back in terms of fantasy points.

Why we're throwing it out: Price is on injured reserve with a chest injury, which knocks this prediction out of contention. Even when he was healthy, Price was a disappointment fantasywise and had fumbling issues.

New bold prediction: Edge rusher Derick Hall will record double-digit sacks for the first time in his career. Hall has two sacks this season along with a 71st percentile pass rush win rate at edge. Hall has recorded a pass rush win rate that high before without getting 10 sacks, but sacks can be somewhat random. If he's winning his reps, that increases his chances at sacks.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Original prediction: Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. will record at least 1,000 receiving yards.

Why we're throwing it out: Godwin has a mere 179 receiving yards over his first five games. I figured that Emeka Egbuka might be limited by the toe injury that was affecting him in the preseason, thus giving a ton of early volume to Godwin. Even though Egbuka has also disappointed, it doesn't seem like the injury is slowing him down or funneling passes to Godwin.

New bold prediction: Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter will make the Pro Bowl. Trotter currently leads all qualifying players in run stop win rate and has recorded a tackle on 18.1% of his defensive snaps, fifth highest in the NFL.

Washington Commanders
Original prediction: Nick Cross will lead all safeties in tackles.

Why we're throwing it out: Cross has only 11 tackles so far this season, trailing far behind the league leader among safeties, the Ravens' Kyle Hamilton (39).

New bold prediction: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt will finish the season with positive rush yards over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. It's bold because Croskey-Merritt is currently at minus-30 for the season. But he just put up plus-40 rush yards over expected in Washington's Week 5 tie with the Giants. I'm buying that he'll continue that positive trend.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid, Barcelona chase Spurs defender Porro
stories.summary: Tottenham defender Pedro Porro is being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Tottenham Hotspur defender Pedro Porro is being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona, while Liverpool have shortlisted Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Tottenham Hotspur right back Pedro Porro is considering leaving the Premier League for a return to Spain, with Barcelona and Real Madrid monitoring his situation. Cadena Ser claims Madrid are leading the race, having monitored him before moving for Denzel Dumfries. Meanwhile, Sport reports that the 27-year-old, who is under contract until 2031, is also of interest to Barca, but the move is dependent on the club freeing up funds, while cheaper alternatives like Iván Fresneda are also being assessed.

- Liverpool have shortlisted Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu as a right-back target for next summer, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Reds admire the France international's versatility alongside Roma's Wesley, though Juventus are actively working to get Kalulu to sign an improved long-term contract.

Arsenal and Aston Villa hold an advantage over Newcastle United in the pursuit of RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa due to offering Champions League football, according to Football Insider. All three clubs are tracking the 21-year-old Norway international after his impressive start to the season saw him bag seven goal contributions in seven appearances.

- Bournemouth have softened their stance and are willing to allow midfielder Alex Scott to leave in January, reports the Daily Mail. However, the Cherries will demand a fee of over £100 million for the 23-year-old's transfer and will only permit a mid-season departure if their Premier League survival remains secure.

- Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, and Everton are keeping tabs on Dinamo Zagreb striker Dion Beljo ahead of a potential January move, per TEAMtalk. The 24-year-old Croatia international has scored 12 goals in his last 14 games, drawing scouting interest from Brentford, Manchester City, and Chelsea as well.

Other rumors
- Chelsea, Bayern Munich, Barcelona and Real Madrid have all added Brighton central defender Luka Vušković to their transfer shortlists ahead of next summer. (Ekrem Konur)

- Viking Stavanger defender Henrik Falchener is attracting interest across Europe after Southampton had a €9.5 million bid to sign him turned down in the summer. (Sky Germany)

- Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are monitoring Manchester United defender Leny Yoro amidst ongoing uncertainty surrounding his long-term future at Old Trafford. (TEAMtalk)

- Chelsea have joined Borussia Dortmund in scouting Philadelphia Union teenager Malik Jakupović, with the MLS club demanding over $10 million as a transfer fee. (TEAMtalk)

- Tottenham Hotspur are considering an €80 million January bid to sign Atlético Madrid midfielder Álex Baena to reinforce their attack following Xavi Simons' injury. (La Razón)

- Crystal Palace defender Jaydee Canvot would welcome a potential transfer to Paris Saint-Germain, though Palace hope to keep the 20-year-old under his contract until 2029. (Football Insider)

- Como midfielder Máximo Perrone is close to extending his contract until 2031 after the Italian club turned down summer inquiries from Inter, Juventus and Napoli. (Nicolò Schira)

- AC Milan defender Fikayo Tomori is edging closer to a departure from San Siro as his contract renewal discussions hit a standstill. (Nicolò Schira)

- Marseille winger Igor Paixão has indicated that a summer exit is far more realistic than a midseason transfer in January. (Canal Plus)

- Tottenham Hotspur, Aston Villa, and Everton are competing to sign Bayer Leverkusen forward Christian Kofane. (Ekrem Konur)

stories.headline: AFL tracker: every player who moved in free agency and the trade period
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Wednesday, Oct. 14
Deadline day
Demons pick up defensive depth with Hawk

Bodie Ryan was a late trade, with the 21-year-old traded from Hawthorn to Melboune in exchange for pick 107 -- a token pick in the end.

Ryan played five games for the Hawks in 2026 but couldn't break into the team ahead of the myriad other medium defenders on the list.

Pedlar makes cross-town switch to Power

It took until the very final minutes, but Luke Pedlar has made the cross-town switch to the Power from the Crows.

Port Adelaide got Pedlar and pick 34, with pick 32 and a 2027 fourth-rounder tied to Richmond going back to Adelaide.

Keidean Coleman gets from Lions to Dons

The deal sees defender Coleman and pick 25 in this year's draft going to Essendon for picks 21 and 27.

Goater traded from North to Hawthorn

Josh Goater, the 22nd pick at the 2021 national draft, has made the move to Hawthorn in exchange for a future third-round pick, tied to Port Adelaide.

Viney and Rivers get to West Coast

Two wantaway Dees have secured their passage west, with Melbourne striking a deal to send Trent Rivers and Jack Viney to the Eagles.

Melbourne gave up Viney, Rivers, and a 2028 second round pick in exchange for West Coast's pick 45, future seconds in 2027 and 2028, and a 2027 fourth round pick.

Will McLachlan becomes a Demon

It took until the final 15 minutes of the trade period, but McLachlan has made his way from Brisbane to the Demons in exchange for pick 45, with a swap of future second-rounders.

McLachlan was pick 6 in the 2024 mid-season draft and played seven games for the Lions.

Tuesday, Oct. 13
Blues land gun Giant

Lachie Whitfield's move to Carlton is official, with the 32-year-old joining the Blues on a three-year deal. Whitfield has played 278 games, and joins Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, and Jake Stringer in departing the Giants.

Carlton receive picks 31 and 50 along with the veteran, with pick 25, pick 26, and a 2028 third-round pick going back the other way.

Former top-five pick on the move

Zane Duursma has got his wish, joining Melbourne along with pick 52. The Roos get pick 33 and 49 in return.

Blues ruck crosses to Collingwood

Flynn Riley has been traded to the Magpies after joining Carlton in the mid-season draft this year, making his AFL debut in Round 18.

A 2028 third-round pick goes the Blues' way.

Swans trade star defender to North Melbourne

The biggest name left on the AFL trade board has tumbled, with Sydney agreeing to move Nick Blakey to North Melbourne.

The Swans offloaded Blakey, draft pick No.52 and their 2028 second-round selection in exchange for a glut of picks.

The Kangaroos traded picks No.6 and No.47, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to get the deal done.

Monday Oct. 12
Suns land Schubert, Butler from Hawks

The Suns have landed their offseason trade target in Aidan Schubert from Hawthorn, in a package also involving Sam Butler and some picks going both ways.

Gold Coast gained Schubert, Butler, Hawthorn's 2028 first-round pick, and Hawthorn's 2027 third-round pick, in exchange for Gold Coast's 2028 first-rounder, and second rounders in both 2027 and 2028.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club.

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Freddy Peralta, Liam Hicks lift the Rays to a 3-1 win over the Guardians that evens the ALCS at 1-1
stories.summary: — With the crowd chanting his name, a fired-up Freddy Peralta pumped one fastball after another past hitters all night long.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- — With the crowd chanting his name, a fired-up Freddy Peralta pumped one fastball after another past hitters all night long.


Peralta threw six innings of four-hit ball, Liam Hicks lined a two-run single after Jos頒am𹑺's fielding error and the Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 Tuesday night to even the AL Championship Series at 1-1.


Game 3 of the best-of-seven series is Thursday night in Cleveland.


Peralta threw the hardest pitch of his big league career at 99.4 mph and relied on his four-seam fastball on 71 of 99 pitches — his 71.7% usage was his highest since June 11, 2019.


“It’s no secret that I trust in my fastball a lot and it’s my best pitch,” Peralta said.


Peralta's 96.9 mph average fastball velocity was 2.6 mph above his season average.


“It plays a big role, the adrenaline,” Peralta said. “And also I define myself as a competitor, and I like these kind of games. I’ve always said in the past, that I enjoyed this as a Dominican pitcher. I grew up watching the games in D.R., and that’s the game that you see. And I got used to that because I grew up watching it. And I feel that I have that in me, in myself. And that’s the way that I feel when I am on the mound in these kind of games.”


Peralta pumped a fist and screamed joyfully walking off the mound in the sixth after fanning Petey Halpin swinging at a 3-2 changeup.


“I just enjoyed the moment because it was a really good at-bat,” Peralta said. “It wasn’t an easy game since the first pitch that I threw until the last one. It was a lot of competition between me and the hitters. ... I think that was why I was fired up like that.”


Ram𹑺, whose two-run homer in Game 5 of their AL Division Series against Chicago helped the Guardians become the 11th team to overcome an 0-2 deficit in a best-of-five series, misplayed a grounder in the fourth inning that led to three unearned runs against rookie lefty Parker Messick.


Junior Caminero walked to start that inning and Victor Mesa Jr. grounded into a forceout originally ruled a double play. The Rays challenged the calls at both first and second and Mesa was ruled safe when a video review overturned the out decision by first base umpire Mark Ripperger.


After Jonny DeLuca struck out, Chandler Simpson beat out a high chopper to shortstop, and the Mesa reached third standing up when Ram𹑺 failed to cover the bag.


Ben Williamson followed with a grounder that scooted underneath Ram𹑺’s glove and between his legs after the ball hit the edge where the artificial turf met the infield dirt. The third baseman played back rather than charging.


“It's a little bit faster here this type of surface,” Ramirez said through a translator. “It's frustrating. I feel bad.”


Williamson reached second and Simpson went to third. Hicks drove the next pitch to right-center for a 3-0 lead, electrifying the towel-waving, cowbell-ringing crowd of 32,125 fans at Tropicana Field.


Peralta and three relievers didn’t need any more support.


“I think the velocity really stood out,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said of Peralta.


Kevin Kelly got two outs in the seventh, retiring Ram𹑺 on a fly ball to center with two runners on.


Lefty Ian Seymour replaced him and Chase DeLauter lined an RBI double to the right-field corner.


Seymour struck out Jo Adell swinging at a changeup, leaving runners at second and third. Seymour pitched a 1-2-3 eighth and Bryan Baker finished with a perfect ninth for his fourth postseason save.


Acquired by the Rays from the Mets at the trade deadline, Peralta turned around his season in Tampa Bay going 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts after posting a 4.99 ERA for New York.


He pitched his latest gem in front of Mets owner Steve Cohen, who was in attendance.


“We have a good relationship,” Peralta said of Cohen. “I think he’s awesome. And I’m happy that he was here watching, not watching me, watching the Rays.”


Messick, who grew up going to Rays games at the Trop, took the loss after giving up six hits and the three unearned runs in five innings.


Cleveland had won four straight in the postseason for the first time since winning their first six playoff games in 2016 on the way to a World Series berth.


The 98-win Rays swept the New York Yankees before a 7-3 loss in Game 1 on Monday.


That was their first loss in two weeks. Now, they're back on the winning track and need three more in a series that's reduced to a best of five to advance to their third World Series.


Liam's lineup drop
After batting cleanup in the first two games against the Yankees and sixth in Game 3 of that series, Hicks wasn't in the lineup against lefty Foster Griffin on Monday and batted eighth against Messick.


He doesn't care where he hits.


“This lineup is so good, you can hit anywhere in the lineup, and you’re not getting offended,” Hicks said. “There’s going to be opportunities.”


No hit for you
Caminero leaped to his left to snag Steven Kwan's hard liner to third in the fifth and then wagged a finger toward the batter. Caminero, who played all 162 games in the regular season and hit 42 home runs, was in the lineup after a collision with DeLuca on a foul ball in the ninth inning Monday night.


Up Next
Rays RHP Griffin Jax (8-10, 3.52 ERA) starts Thursday night. He struck out four and gave up one run in two innings of relief against the Yankees. RHP Gavin Williams (14-8, 3.76) is expected to start for the Guardians. Williams started Games 2 and 5 against the White Sox and tossed an inning in relief in Game 4. He had 24 strikeouts in 11 2/3 innings, allowing two runs and six hits.

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: Why are Shakhtar playing Champions League games at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge?
stories.summary: Explaining why Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk will play home Champions League games at Chelsea's stadium.
stories.body:
Shakhtar Donetsk will host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday but the game will be played nearly 1,700 miles from their Ukraine home.

Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's home stadium, will act as Shakhtar's home ground for their European fixtures this season.

ESPN breaks down why that's happening...

Why are Shakhtar playing at Stamford Bridge?

Shakhtar are based in the Ukrainian city of Donetsk.

But they haven't played at their home ground, the Donbas Arena, since 2014. This year, amid security reasons due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, they were seeking a stadium for their four home fixtures in the league phase of the Champions League.

Shakhtar have recently played 'home' European fixtures in Poland, Slovenia and Germany and were linked with using Brentford's stadium this season, but ended up agreeing to play at Stamford Bridge.

FC Shakhtar said: "Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar. We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue. Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere. We are convinced that Shakhtar's matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans."

The 2021 UK census states that approximately 19,000 Ukraine-born people live in London.

How does it affect Chelsea?

Chelsea have no European fixtures this season after finishing 10th in the Premier League last season.

The Blues even cited their "disappointing 2025-26 season and failure to qualify for European football" as part of their reasoning to welcome Shakhtar.

A Chelsea statement said: "FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year.

"We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters."

What matches will Stamford Bridge host?

Shakhtar vs. AEK Athens, Oct. 14
Shakhtar vs. Sporting CP, Nov. 3
Shakhtar vs. Fenerbahce, Nov. 25
Shakhtar vs. Real Madrid, Jan. 27

Chelsea were owned by Roman Abramovich

Chelsea were formerly owned by Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich.

He was forced to sell the club after 20 years in 2022 under pressure from UK government sanctions after Russia invaded Ukraine.

Where do Shakhtar play home domestic matches?

Shakhtar have largely played their 'home' matches in the Ukrainian league at the Lviv Arena, which is 600 miles from Donetsk, since 2014.

stories.headline: The UFC's flyweights are hot again - is Lone'er Kavanagh the next star?
stories.summary: Could a breakout win at UFC 333 propel Britain's Lone'er Kavanagh into the flyweight title picture?
stories.body:
The fighting life of a UFC flyweight was once an unenvied one.

Constant uncertainty over the future of the division, a lack of big pay-per-view interest and an unfortunate routine of far too many fighters getting cut for the weight class to sustain itself were just some of the problems that characterised the modern era. UFC president Dana White put it in simple terms, saying after Demetrious Johnson's UFC exit in 2018 that "people didn't care" about the flyweights. Even Olympic gold medalist and former two-division champion Henry Cejudo struggled to see how the flyweight division would continue as a part of the UFC, with his own brash persona and entertaining title defences pivotal to maintaining awareness of the division.

Much has changed since the days of Cejudo though, and the flyweights now have a genuine claim to being one of the most exciting divisions in the whole of the UFC. And one man at the forefront of that charge is another promising fighting talent from across the Atlantic, with England's Lone'er Kavanagh enjoying a rise like few others this past year.

He accepted a short-notice fight against ex-champion Brandon Moreno in the lion's den of Mexico City in March and produced one of the most stunning UFC upsets in recent memory, taking the unanimous decision win in front of a hostile crowd. Kavanagh was unranked before that fight and despite more recently losing to Brandon Royval at UFC 329, he remains just a win away from breaking into the flyweight title conversation. Taking on Royval on the night of Conor McGregor's return in Las Vegas in July, Kavanagh was submitted but earned the fight of the night on one of the promotion's most-watched recent cards in a back-and-forth slugfest. The 27-year-old's exciting style and high ceiling was on show that evening and will be again when he faces Ramazonbek Temirov on what is remarkably just his second high-profile numbered event at UFC 333 on Oct. 24.

"Thinking back to certain moments [in Mexico City], it was like a rollercoaster, it was a sick opportunity and I'm glad I did it and my team backed me to do it," Kavanagh tells ESPN.

"[Royval was] another step on the journey, losing is never fun, no matter what stage you're at whether you're at the top or at any point of your career but unfortunately sometimes you have to learn like that -- learning on the go, that's what we're doing right now.

"I believe I've got the best team around me so I truly believe with this team I can make it all the way to the top and that's the plan, that's the aim.

"I'm always trying to work on things from every fight. Unfortunately, you learn a lot more when you lose."

For Kavanagh, the lights have quickly turned brighter. Like many of his British counterparts in the UFC, he was made in Cage Warriors, the organisation that can take credit for the likes of McGregor, Paddy Pimblett and Tom Aspinall. From there, a first round knockout on Dana White's Contender Series saw the journey in the big time begin. His first professional defeat came in the UFC against the experienced Charles Johnson, but that was quickly forgotten with the Moreno heist that saw his stock in the game skyrocket. Kavanagh's front-footed, devious style stemming from his kickboxing roots has even earned him praise from one of the greatest to ever step in the octagon with a Jon Jones Facetime after that UFC Mexico win leaving him "starstruck."

"Your Muay Thai is beautiful, your kicks, they don't show at all. They have no telegraph. It's so nice," Jones said to Kavanagh.

It is a style that was born at London's Great Britain Top Team (GBTT), where alongside UFC veteran Nathaniel Wood and fellow prospect Shanelle Dyer, Kavanagh has honed his craft, going from a five-time K1 kickboxing champion to now potentially a statement win away from challenging for UFC gold under British MMA trailblazer Brad Pickett. And that too in a division where the competition is possibly as fierce as it has ever been. Royval, Tatsuro Tairo, Manuel Kape, Asu Almabayev and bona fide flyweight royalty Alexandre Pantoja make up the spine of a group of challengers that Kananagh finds himself a part of.

Joshua Van's UFC 331 title defence ended any doubts about his validity as champion, with a dominant win over Pantoja, and at just 24-years-old he looks set for a stint at the top -- where Kavanagh aspires to be. But first, No. 7 ranked, one below Kavanagh, and unbeaten in the UFC, the explosive Temirov is one of the toughest challenges the Englishman has faced in his career, and in a weight class as deep as the flyweights, back-to-back losses would see Kavanagh fall mercilessly down the pecking order -- the stakes are high at UFC 333.

"I think the flyweight division is the best division at the moment. It's forever changing," Kavanagh says. "There are so many young up and comers but there are also so many people that have been around for so long. So it's got a good mixture of everything and to be honest, just excited to be a part of it - it's sick being a flyweight at this time.

"I'm a very 'one fight at a time' kind of person, I'll always look at what's in front of me and then what's next but I think it would be an exciting fight either way, [Joshua] Van vs. Lon."

Born in London to an Irish father and Chinese mother, Kavanagh wears his heritage on his sleeve with his name Lone'er translating to "Little Dragon" in English. He credits his mum for pushing him into MMA, a decision that has since paid dividends.

Kavanagh is now set to be a part of a main card alongside two title fights at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. In his way, Uzbekistan's Temirov is coming in red hot on the back of a first-round finish against Steve Erceg, he last tasted defeat in an MMA bout seven years ago and has never been knocked out.

"I haven't seen all the fighters just fighting like me. Just striking punches, just making knockouts. But my punches will just kill them all," Temirov told the UFC.

The kickboxer is aware of the danger that Temirov carries but also the opportunity up for grabs.

"I think a win there puts me right back up there. He's a dangerous opponent. He's got some good wins under him, a lot of wins, but I think a win against him puts me right back up at the top. [I'm] always looking for a finish," Kavanagh said.

"His main weapons are his heavy hands, and that excites me. I love fights like that and I think it's a good fight for me. Hopefully [another fight of the night], I'm looking for more performances of the night."

As is now customary with Kavanagh's UFC bouts, his throwdown against the formidable Temirov is one not to be missed. With the top of the flyweight division so deep he will want to turn all the excitement surrounding him into consistency to earn a shot at Van's belt, that journey will take its latest step in a treacherous division.

And as Bruce Buffer introduces both fighters, perhaps there will be something for the UFC bosses and fans alike to take away before a single punch is even thrown. That all these years after Cejudo and Johnson have been and gone, the flyweights are box office property once again.
